summary: pinochiomathm typosquat fetches, decrypts, and eval()s remote payload on require
details: Package advertises itself as a glob matcher mimicking picomatch/micromatch but on require, index.js loads lib/pinochiomathm.js which stages two base64-encoded files disguised as source-maps (lib/parse.ts.map and lib/init.ts.map), decodes them to lib/parsetmp.js and lib/config.js, requires the decoded module, and unlinks the originals to erase traces. The decoded module fetches an AES-256-CBC-encrypted payload from https://www.jsonkeeper.com/b/V6NBX (base64-hidden in the source), decrypts it with a hardcoded key, and eval()s the plaintext at load time. The C2 URL, header, and password are base64-nested to defeat plain scanning. Since the payload is remote and mutable, arbitrary attacker-controlled code executes on any host that requires this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
